description: The plot illustrates how loss changes over training time for two methods, “Vanilla” and “SepLLM,” shown as two line series on the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 250,000 seconds with regularly spaced tick labels every 50,000 seconds. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with tick labels at 0.05 intervals (2.40, 2.45, …, 2.75). The “Vanilla” series is drawn as a purple solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near the top of the axis around 2.75 at early training times, decreases steadily, is around 2.62 near 50,000 s, around 2.57 near 100,000 s, around 2.54 near 150,000 s, and approaches about 2.50 by roughly 250,000 s. The “SepLLM” series is drawn as a red solid line with circular markers; it begins around 2.71 at early training times, declines smoothly, is around 2.61 near 50,000 s, around 2.56 near 100,000 s, around 2.52 near 150,000 s, reaches about 2.50 around 190,000–200,000 s, and continues slightly below 2.50 (approximately 2.49) by about 230,000–240,000 s. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at loss = 2.50, and a green dashed rectangular annotation highlights a region roughly between 200,000 and 250,000 seconds and between about 2.40 and 2.56 on the loss axis.
